newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q3 GDP rose 2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q3 GDP rose 2.2 pct.

text.p: Commerce seasonally adjusted GDP data on a chain-weighted basis. Following are annualized percent changes from prior quarters, in 1992 chain dollars.
Pct Change,'92 chain dollars: Q3-A---Q2-F---Q1-F---1995 Consumer Spending-Services 1.1 2.7 2.4 2.2
Note: Advance (A) is first estimate, Preliminary (P) is second estimate, and Final (F) is last estimate for the quarter.
Seasonally adjusted annual rates, in blns of '92 chain dollars:
Wall Street economists had expected the initial estimate of third quarter GDP growth to show a 1.8 percent increase.
The 0.3 percent increase in final sales in the third quarter was the weakest performance since the first quarter of 1993, when sales fell 0.9 percent.
The 0.4 percent increase in consumer spending in the third quarter was the weakest since a 1.0 percent drop in the fourth quarter of 1991.
By contrast, the rise in business inventories in the third quarter was the biggest since a $54.5 billion increase in the first quarter of 1991.
On the price front, the 1.9 percent rise in the chain-type price index for all purchases in the third quarter was the smallest since an identical rise in the second quarter of 1994.
The department said the chain-type price index for gross domestic purchases increased 1.8 percent in the third quarter after rising by 2.1 percent in the second quarter.
Excluding food and energy prices, gross domestic purchases prices increased 1.9 percent in the third quarter after rising 1.2 percent in the second quarter, it said.
In compiling the third quarter data, the department made several assumptions about the performance of some components in September.
It assumed that non-motor vehicle inventories increased in September, but at a slower rate than in July and August.

It also assumed that non-gold exports rose in September at a pace about one-third of the increase reported for August. Goods imports were assumed to have fallen in September after rising in July and August, the department said.
